content.text: LATEST Spurs vs. Clippers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/2/26) Pelicans vs. Trail Blazers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/2) Cavaliers vs. Warriors: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/2/26) Mets vs. Giants: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (4/2/26) Braves vs. Diamondbacks: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (4/2) Illinois State vs. Auburn: Predictions, How to Watch for Free (4/2) Lakers vs. Thunder: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/2/26) Frances Tiafoe vs. Rinky Hijikata: Predictions, How to Watch Home » Pistons vs. Wizards: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/19/26) The Detroit Pistons (49–19) face the Washington Wizards (16–52) tonight at Capital One Arena in their second meeting this week. The Pistons will be without superstar Cade Cunningham, who will be out for at least the next two weeks with a collapsed lung. A return in time for the playoffs is possible, but Detroit’s immediate priority is to hold on to the top spot in the Eastern Conference, with the Boston Celtics just 3.5 games behind, with 14 games left in the regular season. Detroit, however, should have no problem tonight in this rematch against a Wizards team they beat on Tuesday, 130–117. Cunningham left that game early with what was described at the time as back spasms. Jalen Duren stepped up, posting a 36-point, 12-rebound double-double. He’s averaging 25.0 PPG over his last six games. The Pistons’ bench also came up big, combining for 62 points. For the Wizards, Bub Carrington led with 30 points on 12-of-16 shooting, draining six 3-pointers. Rookie Will Riley followed with 21 for the second straight game. And Justin Champagnie added 18 points. Prediction Expect another comfortable double-digit win for Detroit, with Duren taking the lead and the bench getting ample minutes against a struggling Wizards squad. Prediction: Detroit Pistons 124, Washington Wizards 109 Injury Report Detroit Pistons Cade Cunningham — Out (Chest) Wendell Moore Jr. — Out (Contract) Isaiah Stewart — Out (Foot) Washington Wizards Bilal Coulibaly — Out (Heel) Leaky Black — Out (Ankle) Trae Young — Out (Quad) Anthony Davis — Out (Finger) Kyshawn George — Out (Elbow) D’Angelo Russell — Out (Not injury related) Cam Whitmore — Out (Venous condition) How to Watch Pistons vs. Wizards Tip-off for tonight’s Pistons-Wizards game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern at the Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. The game airs live locally on FanDuel Sports Network Detroit and Monumental Sports Network. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month. Detroit Pistons vs. Washington Wizards Date: Thursday, March 19, 2026 Time: 7:00 PM Eastern Venue: Capital One Arena TV: FanDuel Sports Network Detroit, Monumental Sports Network Streaming: NBA League Pass (out-of-market) More from Globely News VCU (27–7) faces North Carolina (24–8) tonight in the 2026 NCAA Tournament First Round at Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina. VCU enters the matchup in strong form, having won six straight and 15 of its last 16 games. The Rams secured the Atlantic 10 Tournament title on Sunday with a 70–62 win over Dayton — their sixth consecutive game holding an opponent to 66 points or fewer. Nyk Lewis led the way with 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Terrence Hill Jr. and Michael Belle combined to score 16 points off the bench. VCU shot just 40% from the field overall but was highly efficient from three-point range, converting 46% of its attempts. North Carolina, meanwhile, comes in after an 80–79 loss to Clemson in the ACC Tournament quarterfinals, as a comeback from an 18-point deficit fell just short late. With star freshman Caleb Wilson sidelined for the season, Henri Veesaar delivered a standout performance, posting a 28-point, 17-rebound double-double. Derek Dixon added 16 points, and Seth Trimble finished with 13 points and eight assists. Prediction North Carolina is 5–4 without Wilson, though two of those losses also came while Veesaar was also sidelined. Since Veesaar’s return, the Tar Heels are 4–2, with his interior presence providing stability on both ends. VCU’s defensive pressure and late-season momentum make this a dangerous matchup. An upset is possible, but expect UNC to prevail in a tight contest late. Predicted Final Score: North Carolina 74, VCU 72 How to Watch VCU vs. North Carolina Tip-off for today’s game between VCU and North Carolina is set for 6:50 PM Eastern at Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina. The game airs on TNT and streams live on the TNT app and website, as well as HBO Max. If you’re a cord-cutter without an active livestreaming plan, you can watch the game for free by taking advantage of free trials from DIRECTV STREAM, Hulu + Live TV, or YouTube TV. Hulu + Live TV also includes Disney+ and ESPN Select as part of its standard plan.
